findings.title: Retry cleanup clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.description: The first `deleteMany` now uses `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second branch has no `method` filter, so any `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` is deleted, including non-SMS methods and reminders that are not yet due. The current code path only increments `retryCount` for SMS, so this is latent today, but the delete scope is broader than the original SMS-past-date intent. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retry branch, and consider logging the number of rows deleted by each branch.

findings.title: Unguarded database update in the catch block can abort the loop
findings.description: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block sits outside any try. If that update throws, the error propagates out of the `for` loop, so the remaining reminders in the batch are never processed. Wrap the update in its own try/catch and log the failure, so one bad row cannot stop the batch.

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry behaviour
findings.description: The diff adds `retryCount` persistence in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block, plus a new deletion rule. No test in the diff exercises these paths: a reminder that fails should have its count incremented, a reminder with `retryCount > 1` should be deleted, and a failing update should not stop the batch. Add tests for these cases.

findings.title: Read-modify-write on retryCount is not atomic
findings.description: Both increments use `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, which reads a value fetched earlier in the run. Concurrent runs could lose an increment. Prisma's `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` avoids this and would be simpler.
